forecaster_note: Easing mid-period south swell (more than is showing on the spot forecasts) plus a little bit of east swell should give us some waist to occasionally chest high surf at south magnets, with knee to waist elsewhere. Offshore with clean conditions all day. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: Fresh W offshore 16 gusting 35 km/h through the morning, easing to 14 by midday and 8 by 3pm — groomed but breezy

shark.summary: No shark detections or sightings logged Palm Beach → Manly in the last 24h across the SMART drumline, DPI drone and Surf Life Saving NSW feeds.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small and clean. Energy only reaches 36 kJ around midday and the dominant band is a 2.6ft 4s SW slop-swell — the long-period stuff (0.6ft 12s S, 0.5ft 13s ENE) is background noise. W offshore 16 gusting 35 km/h grooms it all morning, tide runs 0.34m low at 6:28am to 1.46m high at 12:58pm. Longboard or fish tune-up, not a shortboard day.

dee-why.window: 10am–12pm on the pushing tide. POOR-FAIR every hour of the day, so there's no better slot to wait for — go when the tide has some water on the banks.

tip.label: Point is off the table
tip.text: 36 kJ with a 4-second SW as the lead band gives the Point nothing to wrap around — you'd be paddling, not surfing. Take the beachies mid-tide, biggest board you own, and treat any right that stands up as a frontside bonus.

long-reef.window: Same 1–2ft as everywhere else and POOR-FAIR all day. Nothing here today that Dee Why doesn't already give you closer to home.

tip.label: No exposure edge today
tip.text: Long Reef usually buys you extra size from exposure, but with the swell this weak the numbers are identical across all four spots. Save the drive.

curl-curl.window: Pick of the four, but only just — the single FAIR rating on the coast today lands at 6am, then it drops to poor-fair from 9am on.

tip.label: Dawn or don't
tip.text: The south corner takes the SW windswell better than anywhere else, which is why it's the only FAIR reading. That's a 6am window and it closes fast — short, fast lefts, backside for you, so set the rail early off the bottom.

manly.window: Poor-fair all day at 1–2ft. Only worth it if you're already in town.

tip.label: Log it
tip.text: North Steyne sits in the shadow on a SW windswell. Longboard on the incoming tide or nothing.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: A real step up. Energy more than doubles to 84 kJ as a 2ft 10s S teams with a 1.9ft 8s S — FAIR at every spot, 2–3ft, and Long Reef climbing to 3–4ft waist-to-chest. W offshore 11–12 km/h holds the morning then goes light ESE onshore by 3pm. Strictly a morning.

dee-why.window: FAIR from dawn through 3pm. Best 9am–12pm as the energy peaks and the tide pushes to a 1.49m high at 2pm.
alerts: Wind flips light ESE onshore around 3pm

long-reef.window: Biggest on the coast at 3–4ft and FAIR all day. Go 9–11am before the W offshore goes cross-shore at midday.
alerts: W goes cross-shore here from noon

curl-curl.window: FAIR all day, offshore until 3pm. Solid backup to Long Reef and the south corner will hold the S swell shape.
alerts: Wind flips light ESE onshore around 3pm

manly.window: Smallest of the four at 1–2ft and slips to poor-fair by 3pm. Bottom of the list.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday: 80 kJ off a 3.3ft 8s S at 178° — that's dead south, which wraps badly into Dee Why. Long Reef at 3–4ft is the call, and the ENE onshore arrives by 3pm. Sunday is the week: 170 kJ with a 3.2ft 9s ENE at 70°, exactly the direction Dee Why wants, under NNW–N offshore. Long Reef is the only FAIR-GOOD reading on the board. Sunday mid-morning is the session.

dee-why.window: Sat: FAIR to 9am only — the dead S at 178° doesn't wrap in here, and the NNE goes onshore by noon. Sun: FAIR all day, and the ENE 70° is the one direction the Point actually likes. Get on it 9–11am.
alerts: Sat swell is dead S (178°) — poor wrap into Dee Why
Sun N wind 18 gusting 34 km/h reads cross-shore here from 9am

tip.label: Sunday mid-morning, Point
tip.text: 170 kJ on a 9s ENE at 70° sits right in the 30–80° band the Point needs, and it's the highest energy reading of the week by a factor of two. Frontside rights on the pushing tide, 9–11am. If you surf once this week, make it this.

long-reef.window: Best of the weekend both days. Sat FAIR all day at 3–4ft; Sun FAIR-GOOD at dawn, 9am and again at 3pm, with N offshore holding all day.

tip.label: The safe bet
tip.text: Only FAIR-GOOD rating on the board this week, and the headland keeps the Sunday NNW offshore here while it goes cross at Dee Why. If the wind is already up when you look out the window, come here instead.

curl-curl.window: Sat FAIR to noon at 2–3ft then POOR by 3pm as the ENE fills in. Sun FAIR all day at 3–4ft with N offshore — the most consistent rating of the two days.
alerts: Sat drops to POOR by 3pm on the ENE onshore

manly.window: Sat 2–3ft, FAIR early then poor-fair from noon. Sun 2–4ft FAIR but the N wind is cross-shore here all day.
alerts: Sun N wind cross-shore all day at North Steyne
